t: The provisions of section 19(m) of the Federal Non-Nuclear Energy Research and Development Act of 1974, as amended, shall not apply to alternative fuels actions under Public Law 96–126 and Public Law 96–304.

fable.w: This section only exempts certain alternative fuels actions from an existing statutory provision. It creates no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, rulemaking, or right to sue. The tempting reading is that the cross-referenced section 19(m) might involve some procedural requirement, but the text here only makes that provision inapplicable and brings no non-federal party into a federal decision.
fable.s: shall not apply to alternative fuels actions under Public Law 96–126 and Public Law 96–304

qwen_block.w: This section is a purely procedural exclusion that removes the applicability of a specific statutory provision to certain actions. It does not establish any mechanism for consultation, public comment, advisory boards, or coordination with outside parties. It merely defines the scope of existing regulations.
qwen_block.s: The provisions of section 19(m) of the Federal Non-Nuclear Energy Research and Development Act of 1974, as amended, shall not apply to alternative fuels actions under Public Law 96–126 and Public Law 96–304.

opus.w: This section only exempts alternative fuels actions from another statute's provision. It creates no process for anyone outside the federal government to take part in a federal decision. The word 'actions' and the cross-reference to another Act may look procedural, but nothing in the text involves states, the public, experts or other outside parties. Based on recall rather than the text, the provision being switched off also appears to concern Congress, which is inside the federal government.
opus.s: The provisions of section 19(m) of the Federal Non-Nuclear Energy Research and Development Act of 1974, as amended, shall not apply to alternative fuels actions under Public Law 96–126 and Public Law 96–304.
opus.b:
1. **Reading.** One could be tempted to call this participation because it mentions "alternative fuels actions" and switches off a procedural provision of another Act. That reading fails. On its face, the section only says that section 19(m) does not apply. It names no party outside the federal government and sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body or right to sue. From memory, section 19(m) deals with limits on loan guarantees tied to congressional authorization, so even the provision being switched off would stay inside the federal government. The section text itself does not confirm that.

2. **Label.**

qwen_chat.w: This section merely states that a specific provision of another act does not apply to certain actions. It does not create any requirement for consultation, public comment, advisory committees, or other forms of participation with outside parties. It is a negative declaration regarding the applicability of existing law, not an affirmative mandate for engagement.
qwen_chat.s: The provisions of section 19(m) of the Federal Non-Nuclear Energy Research and Development Act of 1974, as amended, shall not apply to alternative fuels actions under Public Law 96–126 and Public Law 96–304.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the section references "alternative fuels actions" under other laws, it implicitly involves participation mechanisms defined in those laws. However, this section itself only excludes certain provisions from applying; it does not establish, require, or describe any participation process. It is a purely procedural exclusion clause.
